what: The Metronome plays a steady click so you can practise music, dance or exercise in time. You can set any tempo from 20 to 300 beats per minute (BPM).

Choose a time signature such as 3/4, 4/4 or 6/8, accent the first beat of each bar, add quieter clicks between the beats, and pick a sound. Each beat lights up in a row of circles, and you can make any beat accented, normal or silent.
The clicks are scheduled ahead of time on your device's audio clock with the Web Audio feature, which keeps the timing steady and accurate.
uses: Build speed on scales and difficult passages a few BPM at a time.
Keep a steady tempo while learning a song.
Practise grooves with eighth or sixteenth note subdivisions.
Set a tempo for steps, skipping or running cadence.
Tap along with a song to find its BPM.
Use the visual beat on a big screen in class.
tutorial: Drag the slider, press − or + (hold them to change quickly), or type a number from 20 to 300 in the "Tempo" box. The Italian tempo name, such as Andante or Allegro, appears under the number.
Press "Tap tempo" in time with the music at least twice. The tempo is set from the average of your taps.
Pick 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8 and others. The circles show the beats of one bar.
Leave "Accent the first beat" on for a stronger first beat. Tap any circle to switch it between accented, normal and silent.
Under "Clicks between beats" choose 2, 3 or 4 for softer in-between clicks. Choose Click, Beep, Wood block or Hi-hat, and set the volume.
Press Start or the space bar. The current bar and beat are shown, and the circles light up. Tick "Flash the screen on the first beat" for a stronger visual cue.
features: Slider, buttons, typing or tap tempo.
Scheduled on the audio clock, steady even in a busy page.
Tap a beat to change it.
Lit-up circles and an optional flash, good for deaf or hard-of-hearing players and noisy rooms.

example.title: Worked example: speeding up a scale
example.text: Hassan is learning a fast scale on the guitar. He sets the tempo to 80 BPM, keeps 4/4 and chooses "2 (eighth notes)" so he hears two clicks per beat, matching his two notes per beat. He presses Start and plays the scale ten times cleanly, then presses + five times to reach 85 BPM. Over a week he works up to 120 BPM, raising it by 5 each time he can play it without mistakes.

tips: Practise slowly first: if you make mistakes, lower the tempo by 10 BPM.
Make beat 1 silent sometimes, so you learn to feel the bar yourself.
Use the space bar to start and stop with your hands free from the mouse.
On iPhone, switch off silent mode or you will not hear the clicks.
Use headphones in noisy rooms, or the visual beat if you cannot use sound.
problems: Check the volume slider and your device volume. On iPhone, turn off silent mode. Then press Start again.
The clicks stop when the screen turns off
Phones pause web pages to save power. Keep the screen on; the tool asks to keep it awake while playing where possible.
Tap at least twice, and tap within 2 seconds of each other. Taps slower than 20 BPM or faster than 300 BPM are not used.
The tempo box goes back to a number
Only 20 to 300 BPM are allowed; a number outside is set to the nearest limit.
